newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait 1997/98 oil income calculated at $13/bl.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait 1997/98 oil income calculated at $13/bl.

text.p: Oil revenue in Kuwait's 1997/98 budget is calculated at a conservative $13 a barrel, parliament was told on Tuesday.

"Oil revenue is estimated at two million barrels per day (Kuwait's OPEC quota) at $13 a barrel in line with the principle of caution when calculating oil revenue which is estimated at 2.555 billion dinars ($8.391 billion)," the financial committee said in its presentation of the draft budget.
Parliament is expected to approve the budget on Tuesday for the fiscal year which started July 1, 1997 ahead of a summer recess. The budget has been passed by the financial committee.
Non-oil income is projected at 550 million dinars in the 4.378 billion proposed budget which carries a gross deficit of 1.584 billion dinars.
Each $1 rise in world oil prices above the conservative $13 forecast would result in an increase in Kuwait's annual revenue of 200 million dinars, the finance committee report said.

The 4.21 billion dinar 1996/97 budget carried a projected gross deficit of 1.51 billion which was cut considerably by a rise in oil prices in 1996 by some $5 a barrel above budget forecasts, officials and economists said.
Actual figures for the fiscal year which ended June 30, 1997 have not been released yet.
